title: 它们为什么一起走
subtitle: 一串脚印看出来的事
character: wearing a dusty blue t-shirt, sand coloured shorts and white sneakers, short black hair
style: children's picture book illustration, soft pastel drawing with powdery blended strokes and visible grain, dusty blue, warm clay and pale sand

pages.zh:
博物馆的地上
铺着一块大石板，
上面一个个坑。
爸爸说那是脚印，
恐龙踩出来的。
pages.scene: A medium shot of the little boy seen from his knees up standing on a big flat slab of rock covered in large dinosaur tracks, his face turned towards the viewer, drawn with the natural body proportions of a real five-year-old child, his head in proportion to his body and about one fifth of his height, not a big-headed cartoon, his eyes calm and natural, surprised.

pages.zh:
最大的那个脚印
比脸盆还大，
我整个人坐进去
还空出一圈。
那是后脚踩的。

脚印有两种，
一大一小。
大的是后脚，
小的是前脚。
它是四条腿走路的。

这样的脚印不止一串。
二十几串排在一起，
一串挨着一串，
而且全都朝着
同一个方向去。
pages.scene: Many rows of large round dinosaur tracks pressed into flat rock on a cream background, all the rows running in the same direction. Nothing else in the picture.

pages.zh:
没有哪一串
压在另一串上面，
谁也没踩着谁。
这说明它们
是同时走过去的。

再看得仔细些：
大脚印走在两边，
小脚印夹在中间。
大的在外面，
小的在里面。

外面才有危险。
大的走在外圈，
小的走在当中，
这样就不容易
被谁叼走。
pages.scene: A group of long-necked dinosaurs walking together across open ground on a cream background, the largest ones on the outside and the smaller ones in the middle. Nothing else in the picture.

pages.zh:
量一量两个脚印
中间隔多远，
就能算出来，
它当时走得多快。
答案是：不快。

这一串脚印
是踩在湿泥上的。
太阳晒了几天，
泥就变硬，
后来变成了石头。
pages.scene: One large round dinosaur track pressed deep into wet mud on a cream background, water gathering in the bottom of it. Nothing else in the picture.

pages.zh:
它们一起走，
是要换个地方。
一片树叶吃光了，
就往前挪一挪，
再找一片。

也不是都这样。
有的石头上
从头到尾只有一串，
孤零零的，
那是自己走的。
pages.scene: One single line of large round dinosaur tracks crossing flat rock on a cream background, with no other tracks anywhere. Nothing else in the picture.

pages.zh:
我踩在脚印里，
一步一步往前走。
一亿年前，
这里真的走过
一大群恐龙。
pages.scene: A medium shot of the little boy seen from his knees up standing with one foot inside a huge dinosaur track in the rock, his face turned towards the viewer, drawn with the natural body proportions of a real five-year-old child, his head in proportion to his body and about one fifth of his height, not a big-headed cartoon, his eyes calm and natural, smiling.
